summary: Live bench of the myiotsan Flow Engine's JavaScript sandbox (tools/fleetbench/bench_iotsan_flows.py) against a real broker, driving what a flow's arbitrary-JavaScript nodes can REACH and what they can COST. The sandbox containment itself held completely - no filesystem/network/require escape, no cross-flow scratchpad leakage, a throwing node only drops its own branch - but the bench found real defects on the cost side. A function/expression/switch node's script used to be validated only at runtime compile, so a typo saved, enabled, listed as 'On' on the flows list, and simply never ran, with a single INFO log line as the only trace; scripts are now compiled at SAVE (a shared nodeScript/checkScripts helper the runtime also compiles, so save and runtime can never disagree) and refused with a 400. flowScriptTimeout (100ms) fenced one script call but nothing fenced an EVENT, so a graph of individually well-behaved scripts could legally spend up to 200 nodes x 100ms = 20s of the ONE shared flow worker on a single reading - measured live at 15.1s for a 190-node graph, stalling every other flow in the install; a new flowEventBudget (1s) now bounds one reading's total cost across the whole graph, and a flow whose script TIMES OUT (not merely throws - an ordinary thrown error is free and does not count) 5 times in a row is quarantined and named in the notification feed until it is edited and re-saved. A stale goja watchdog interrupt could also kill the NEXT, unrelated script if a call finished in the same instant its own watchdog fired; the interrupt is now cleared on the way in as well as the way out. Flow rows now carry a runtimeState (running/error/quarantined/disabled/starting) so 'enabled' and 'actually running' are no longer indistinguishable on screen, and a new GET /api/flows/stats endpoint plus three Prometheus gauges (myiotsan_flow_events_dropped_total, myiotsan_flow_queue_depth, myiotsan_flows_stopped) expose the runtime's dropped-event counter, which used to be written to a field nothing ever read (and was a data race, now atomic). Chasing why an install's 110 enabled flows compiled only 100 traced back one layer down to infra/db/sql, shared by every app: all three drivers (sqlite, postgres, mariadb) hardcoded a 100-row scan ceiling in selectWithSQL regardless of the caller's limit, while the reported total row count still reflected the true, larger result - so a truncated page was indistinguishable from a complete one. Roughly seventy call sites across the suite ask for more than 100 rows; the scan now takes exactly the limit the caller asked for, falling back to the historical 100-row ceiling only when no limit was given at all. 41/41 with all fixes; 32/43 against unfixed main on the identical bench file.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change. A flow whose script fails to compile is now refused at save (400) rather than silently accepted - this only affects a NEW save/edit of a broken script, not existing stored flows, which keep running exactly as before until edited. Existing flows well under the new 1s per-event budget and 5-consecutive-timeout quarantine threshold see no behavior change at all. GET /api/flows and GET /api/flows/{id} responses gain two new fields (runtimeState, runtimeDetail) that existing callers can ignore; GET /api/flows/stats is a new endpoint. Three new Prometheus gauges appear on /metrics when telemetry is enabled (the existing default); no config changes required. The infra/db/sql fix changes read behavior for every app: any list query that previously silently truncated to 100 rows while asking for more now returns up to the full limit requested, which is strictly more data, not less, and no caller-visible contract changes (a caller that asked for limit=0 still gets the historical 100-row ceiling, unchanged).
